title: Group of Monuments at Hampi
description: Extensive ruins of the Vijayanagara imperial capital along the Tungabhadra River, featuring the Vittala Stone Chariot, Virupaksha Temple, and medieval waterworks.
altText: Sunrise panorama of the Vittala Temple stone chariot and granite mandapas at Hampi.
historicalBackground: Flourished from the 14th to 16th centuries CE; inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1986 (Reference No. 241) across 4,187.24 hectares.

title: Chennakesava Temple, Belur (Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas)
description: 12th-century Hoysala chloritic schist temple built under King Vishnuvardhana, famed for star-shaped plinths, lathe-turned columns, and signed sculptures.
altText: Chennakesava Temple in Belur showing stellate plinth and carved Hoysala friezes.
historicalBackground: Inscribed alongside Halebidu and Somnathapura on the UNESCO World Heritage List on September 18, 2023 (Reference No. 1670).

title: Badami Rock-Cut Cave Temples
description: Four Early Chalukyan rock-cut sandstone sanctuaries overlooking Agastya Lake, illustrating the foundational synthesis of Nagara and Dravida temple forms.
altText: Red sandstone cliffs and rock-cut verandahs of Badami Cave Temples above Agastya Lake.
historicalBackground: Carved between the 6th and 8th centuries CE under Early Chalukya patronage; Cave 3 preserves an inscription dated 578 CE.
